content:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: 1855000123 - Cross-region failover detected. Automated failover from us-east-1 -> us-west-2 triggered due to network partition affecting us-east-1 AZs. Impact: elevated 5xx for several routes. Paging oncall.
jamal: I’m on it. Observed route flap at 03:14 UTC, target weight shift started by autoscaler/failover policy. Error spike: 502/504s up to 12% p50 latencies +120ms in us-west-2. Repro: curl to public edge returns 502 intermittently.

alex: Confirming BGP reachability hiccup between us-east-1 and our transit peers — traceroutes from edge to us-east show timeouts past the regional gateway. Cloud provider console shows networking incidents in us-east-1b.

maria: Health checks in Route53 started failing for several origin targets in us-east-1; Route53 health evaluator started diverting weight to us-west-2 per policy. TTL is 60s, so clients saw shift fast.

ops-oncall: Customer reports from EU: some sessions routed to us-west-2 where backend pool was underprovisioned for that UE distribution. CPU on inference hosts spiked to 95% in us-west-2; EV Cache misses increased — KV cache warming not ready for sudden load.

jamal: Timeline summary: 03:12 UTC network partition in us-east-1 -> 03:13 health checks fail -> 03:14 automated traffic shift -> 03:15 error spike in us-west-2. Root cause hypothesis: provider AZ networking issue + Route53 failover policy + insufficient cold capacity in failover region.

alex: I’m opening cloud provider ticket (support case 123456789). Also checking if any cross-region peering changed. For now, suggestion: pause automatic weight changes and manually set weights to 70/30 (us-west-2/us-east-1) to reduce churn while we assess.

maria: Command to pause DNS automation (internal tool):

```
# disable auto-weight during incident
./infra/dns-control set-auto-weighting --env prod --enabled false --note "Incident 1855000123"
```

jamal: Doing LB/ALB manipulation now: temporarily add more instances in us-west-2 and start draining noisy origins that keep failing. Commands run:

```
aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name rw-inference-west-2-asg --desired-capacity 40 --region us-west-2
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/worker --replicas=30 --context=west-2
kubectl -n inference cordon node ip-10-0-7-42 && kubectl -n inference drain node ip-10-0-7-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

jamal: After scale up, error rate dropped to ~4% but latencies still high. Looks like KV cache warming is the bottleneck. Cache warmers kicked but need time.

emily: Customer Ops: we have 12 customer tickets flagged as high-impact (session timeouts, truncated responses). Notifying top-10 paying customers and offering status update. Draft status: "We experienced cross-region routing issues and an automated failover that caused elevated errors for some users. We're mitigating by scaling the failover region and pausing automated DNS shifts. Next update in 30m." Any wording changes?

alex: That wording is good. Add that we’ve opened a cloud provider ticket and are monitoring for route reconciliation.

maria: Recommendation: increase Route53 health check grace period and set a higher failover threshold to prevent oscillation on next incident. Action item: postmortem with concrete TTL/threshold changes.

ops-oncall: Repro note for on-call handoffs: if you see automated failover and the target region’s CPU > 85% within 5 minutes, suspend failover and scale up before shifting more traffic. Add to runbook.

jamal: I’ll prepare the immediate mitigations list for the handoff to night oncall in 45m:
- Pause DNS auto-weighting (done)
- Manually set Route53 weights: us-west-2 65, us-east-1 35 (in progress)
- Scale up west-2 ASG (done)
- Start cache warmer jobs (in progress)
- Open cloud ticket and attach traceroutes/logs (alex)
- Notify customers (emily)

sre-bot: Incident severity set to Sev2. Handoff required at 04:00 UTC. Please update status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1855000123

maria: Adding runbook excerpt for postmortem. We should consider: TTL 60s is aggressive for failover policies where backend warmup is non-trivial. Proposed change: TTL 300s + higher evaluation window, and a two-step failover (weighting ramp) rather than instantaneous 100% failover.

alex: Provider update: case 123456789 indicates packet drops in peering fabric affecting egress from us-east region. ETA unknown. They’ve asked for BGP logs, which I’ve uploaded.

ops-oncall: Quick check: are any customers using pinned IP addresses or low DNS TTLs causing them to reconnect mid-transition? emily: some customers pinned IPs for legacy whitelisting. We'll coordinate bespoke IP-level failback with them.

jamal: Observability checklist for post-incident: attach TRACE samples showing failed sessions, list of ALBs that served 502s, Route53 health check history, TTL change logs, and autoscaler decision trace. I’ll capture and upload to the incident doc.

emily: Status update posted to affected customers and status page. I’m marking high-touch customers for follow-up tomorrow.

ops-oncall: Current state at 03:57 UTC: error rate ~3.1% across affected routes, latencies slowly decreasing. Manual weight at 65/35. Autoscaling stable. No new failover events in last 15 minutes.

jamal: Preparing handoff notes for night oncall. Key points: manual control over DNS automation, thresholds to change, scaling steps documented, provider case ID. Handoff in 3 minutes.

alex: Logging provider ticket updates here as they arrive.

sre-bot: @oncall Reminder: please acknowledge handoff in thread.

ops-oncall: Acknowledged. I’m taking over. I’ll monitor BGP, Route53, autoscaler, and customer tickets.

jamal: Thanks team. Postmortem owner: jamal. Timeline and action items will be drafted by EOD UTC.
